BURHAN:v1p179#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r2.claim: Seven sūras instead open with a conditional, introduced as the sixth mode of sūra opening.
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r2.anchor: السادس الشرط نحو ﴿ إذا وقعت الواقعة ﴾ ﴿ إذا جاءك المنافقون ﴾

ITQAN:v4p438/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p438/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p438/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that whoever recites al-Waqi'a every night will never suffer poverty.
ITQAN:v4p438/r4.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي والحارث بن أبي أسامة وأبو عبيد عن ابن مسعود ( من قرأ كل ليلة سورة الواقعة لم تصبه فاقة أبدا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r1.claim: The surah explains the three groups described in al-Raḥmān: the foremost and later believers, and opposing people, including open and hidden hypocrites among humans and jinn.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r1.anchor: شرح أحوال الأقسام الثلاثة المذكورة في الرحمن للأولياء من السابقين واللاحقين والأعداء المشاققين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r2.claim: Its distinctions among people demonstrate complete, freely exercised power; equal outcomes would give naturalists a false objection to divine wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r2.anchor: ولو استوى الناس لم يكن ذلك من بليغ الحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r3.claim: The surah ends by denying every defect and affirming the full majesty and beauty of divine perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r3.anchor: بالتنزيه بالنفي لكل شيء به نقص ثم الإثبات بوصف العظمة بجميع الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r4.claim: The name al-Wāqiʿa signals the surah’s subject when its verses and their temporal relationships are considered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r4.anchor: واسمها الواقعة دال على ذلك بتأمل آياته وما يتعلق الظرف به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#s056/r5.claim: The basmalah portrays God as differentiating human conditions, broadly granting expression, and drawing His party near through beautiful words and deeds.

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r1.speaker: all commentators
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r1.claim: All commentators classify al-Waqiah as Makkan, though some place verses 81–82 or verse 83 in the Madinan period.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r1.anchor: commentators consider al-Wāqiʿah to be a Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r3.claim: The surah takes its name from the Event in verse 1, meaning the Day of Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r3.anchor: takes its name from the mention of the Event in v. 1, a reference to the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r5.claim: Five overlapping sections cover Judgment's signs, the three groups' destinies, proofs of resurrection, the revelation, and death and the Afterlife.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r5.anchor: The sūrah comprises five overlapping sections

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r6.claim: A well-known hadith promises that whoever recites al-Waqiah every night will never be afflicted by need.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r6.anchor: According to a well-known ḥadīth, “Whosoever recites Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah every night shall never be afflicted by need”

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r7.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r7.claim: Ibn Ajibah explains the recitation's promised protection as arising because understanding the surah's teachings on the Hereafter prompts preparation for it.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r7.anchor: Ibn ʿAjībah states that this is because whoever understands the things mentioned in this sūrah regarding the Hereafter will set about preparing for it

STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r8.claim: This attributed virtue has made the surah widely recited at significant moments, especially for the dying or recently dead.
STUDYQURAN:56:intro/r8.anchor: one of the most often recited

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r1.claim: This is the seventh and final Makkan sūrah in its group, closing the Makkan portion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r1.anchor: This is the seventh sūrah of this group and on it ends its Makkan sūrahs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r2.claim: The sūrah sums up the reward-and-punishment discussion from Qāf through al-Raḥmān, replacing prior detailed arguments with the certain outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r2.anchor: the entire discussion regarding reward and punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r3.claim: Earlier sūrahs grounded the case in reason, human nature, and evidence from the inner and outer worlds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r3.anchor: arguments based on human intellect and human nature as well as on the world within a person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r5.claim: Verses 1–10 assert the certain arrival of Judgment, which evaluates faith and deeds and divides humanity into three groups.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p135/r5.anchor: The Day shall evaluate a person according to his faith and deeds; it shall upgrade many a people and downgrade many

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p137/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p137/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p137/r1.claim: Calling the Judgment the al-wāqiʿah conveys that its occurrence is certain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p137/r1.anchor: refers to the Day of Judgement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r1.claim: Arguments for Judgment have already been given and disbelievers’ objections answered; they cannot escape the certain event, so must prepare for a favorable outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r1.anchor: they shall not be able to run away from it in any way

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r2.claim: The word waqiʿatiha is a verbal noun like ʿāqibah and ʿāfiyah, stressing that the event’s occurrence is entirely doubtless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r2.anchor: It means that there is absolutely no doubt in its happening

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r3.claim: The threat is no false warning: the event will come, and people seeking a favorable fate should prepare for it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p138/r3.anchor: there is not a bit of falsehood in it

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan according to reports from Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn al-Zubayr; some except the verses about the two groups of predecessors and later people.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r1.anchor: مكية كما أخرجه البيهقيفي الدلائل وغيره عن ابن عباس وابن مردويه عن ابن الزبير واستثنى بعضهم قوله تعالى : ( ثلة الأولين وثلة من الآخرين )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r2.speaker: مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r2.claim: Some also except the passage about the stars’ settings through the challenge to deniers, based on Muslim’s report about its occasion of revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r2.anchor: وكذا استثنى قوله سبحانه : ( فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم ) إلى ( تكذبون ) لما أخرجهمسلمفي سببنزوله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ al-Bayān reports that Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada excepted the verse about making one’s provision denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r3.anchor: وفيمجمع البيان حكاية استثناء قوله تعالى : ( وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون ) عن ابن عباس وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r4.claim: The surah has ninety-nine verses in the Hijazi and Syrian counts, ninety-seven in the Basran count, and ninety-six in the Kufan count.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r4.anchor: وعدد آيها تسع وتسعون في الحجازي والشامي وسبع وتسعون في البصري وست وتسعون في الكوفي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r5.claim: Al-Raḥmān and al-Wāqiʿah both describe Resurrection, Paradise, and Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r5.anchor: وهي وسورة الرحمن متواخية في أن في كل منهما وصف القيامة والجنة والنار

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r6.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r6.claim: Al-Baḥr links this surah to the prior one’s punishment of criminals and bliss of believers, including two ranks of believers; this surah opens by naming the right-hand, left-hand, and foremost.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r6.anchor: وقالفي البحر : مناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تضمن العذابللمجرمين والنعيم للمؤمنين وفاضلسبحانه بين جنتي بعضالمؤمنين وجنتي بعض آخر منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r7.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r7.claim: Some scholars link ‘when the Event occurs’ with the prior surah’s sky-splitting, treating the surahs as closely joined: one mentions the earth’s shaking and the other the sky’s splitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r7.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة أنظر إلى اتصال قوله تعالى : ( إذاوقعت الواقعة ) بقوله سبحانه : ( فإذاانشقت السماء )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r8.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r8.claim: The two surahs reverse their sequences: al-Raḥmān moves from Qur’an, sun and moon, plants, humanity and jinn, Resurrection, Fire, then Garden; al-Wāqiʿah begins with Resurrection, Garden, Fire, humanity, plants, water, fire, stars, and balance.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r8.anchor: فافتتح في سورة الرحمن بذكر القرآن ثم ذكر الشمس والقمر ثم ذكر النبات ثم خلق الإنسان والجان ثمصفة يوم القيامة ثم صفة النار ثم صفة الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r9.claim: The sequence makes al-Wāqiʿah a counterpart to al-Raḥmān, returning the end of one to the beginning of the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر الميزان فكانت هذه كالمقابلة لتلكو كالمتضمنة لرد العجز على الصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports hearing the Prophet say that reciting al-Wāqiʿah every night prevents poverty forever; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r1.anchor: عنابنمسعود قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول : من قرأسورة الواقعة كل ليلة لم تصبه فاقة أبدا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported with a similar Prophetic narration about reciting the surah nightly to avert poverty; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن عساكر عن ابن عباس نحوه مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r3.claim: Anas reports the Prophet calling al-Wāqiʿah ‘wealth’ and urging its recitation and teaching to children; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن أنسعن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : سورة الواقعة الغنى فاقرءوها وعلموها أولادكم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r4.claim: Al-Dailami reports from Anas a Prophetic instruction to teach al-Wāqiʿah to women because it is a surah of wealth; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p128#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عنه مرفوعاعلمو نسائكم سورة الواقعة فإنها سورة الغنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وعطاء وجابر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, Ikrima, Ata, and Jabir classify Surat al-Waqiʿa as Meccan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445/r1.anchor:
سورة الواقعة
مكية في قول الحسن وعكرمة وعطاء وجابر ،

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.claim: The previous sūra recounts blessings and demands gratitude rather than denial; this one describes good recompense for the grateful and bad recompense for those who deny.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.anchor: تلك السورة مشتملة على تعديد النعم على الإنسان ومطالبته بالشكر ومنعه عن التكذيب

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.claim: The previous sūra points to blessings for servants, while this one similarly points to their recompense on the Day of Calling.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.anchor: ثانيها : أن تلك السورة متضمنة للتنبيهات بذكر الآلاء في حق العباد ، وهذه السورة كذلك لذكر الجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.claim: The previous sūra displays mercy, whereas this one displays awe, reversing the pattern found between the previous sūra and its own predecessor.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.anchor: ثالثها : أن تلك السورة سورة إظهار الرحمة وهذه السورة سورة إظهار الهيبة على عكس تلك السورة

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.claim: The previous sūra ends with divine attributes stated by affirmation and negation; this one opens with resurrection, reward, and punishment, and both point to God’s majesty, power, and sovereign might.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.anchor: ففي آخر تلك السورة إشارة إلى الصفات من باب النفي والإثبات ، وفي أول هذه السورة إلى القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.claim: One reading takes “the event” as the Resurrection or its earthquake: everyone will acknowledge it, denial will fail, unbelievers will be lowered in Hell, and believers raised in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : المراد إذا وقعت القيامة الواقعة أو الزلزلة الواقعة يعترف بها كل أحد ، ولا يتمكن أحد من إنكارها

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.claim: A second reading says the event shakes people, lowering what is high and raising what is low, signaling its severity and leveling the land and mountains.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : { وقعت الواقعة } تزلزل الناس ، فتخفض المرتفع ، وترفع المنخفض

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.claim: The leveling image is compared to the destruction of Sodom and supported by the next verses about the earth’s violent shaking and the mountains being pulverized; wind also reshapes sandy ground.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا فهي كقوله تعالى : { فجعلنا عاليها سافلها } ( الحجر : 74 ) في الإشارة إلى شدة الواقعة

RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r8.claim: A third reading says the event will be undeniable and without false report or misleading interpretation; “lowering, raising” is coordinated with “false,” conveying that none can reverse the event’s effects.
RAZI-FULL:v29p122#2/r8.anchor: فلا يوجد لها كاذبة ولا متأول يظهر فقوله : { خافضة رافعة } معطوف على { كاذبة } نسقا

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r1.claim: Al-wāqiʿa may modify an omitted Resurrection or earthquake.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون الواقعة صفة لمحذوف وهي القيامة أو الزلزلة

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r2.claim: Alternatively, the omitted noun is an unspecified event, with the feminine ending signaling its gravity and terror.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المحذوف شيئا غير معين ، وتكون تاء التأنيث مشيرة إلى شدة الأمر الواقع وهوله

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r3.claim: The emphatic wording of al-wāqiʿa conveys an event exceeding the bare fact that something happened, as in kānat al-kāʾina.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r3.anchor: كانت الكائنة والمراد كان الأمر كائنا ما كان

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r4.claim: Like rāwiya and nassāba, a final hāʾ can compress an added intensive description into one letter; here the intensification is semantic, despite feminine agreement in the verb.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r4.anchor: نأتي بحرف نيابة عن كلمة كما أتينا بهاء التأنيث

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r5.claim: One analysis makes a preceding verb, اذكر, govern idhā as an object rather than a temporal adverb.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r5.anchor: فعل متقدم يجعل إذا مفعولا به لا ظرفا وهو اذكر

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r6.claim: A second analysis makes laysa liwaqʿatihā kādhiba the governor of idhā.

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r7.claim: A third analysis supplies the day when people are lowered and raised, indicated by khāfiḍa rāfiʿa.
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r7.anchor: يخفض قوم ويرفع قوم ، وقد دل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p123/r8.claim: Another proposed governor is the statement about the people of the right, understood as occurring on the day the Event occurs.

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa and Muhammad hold that seeking refuge in prayer is for Quran recitation, not for the prayer itself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد أنه لأجل القراءة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.claim: Abu Yusuf holds that seeking refuge is for the prayer itself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.anchor: وعند أبي يوسف أنه لأجل الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa and Muhammad say a follower behind the imam does not seek refuge because he does not recite; they rely on the verse conditioning refuge on Quran recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.anchor: عندهما لا يتعوذ لأنه لا يقرأ وعنده يتعوذ وجه قولهما قوله تعالى : ﴿ فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.claim: Abu Yusuf says the follower does seek refuge, since refuge follows the prayer and is repeated with each prayer; if it served recitation, it would recur with each recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.anchor: وجه أبي يوسف أن التعوذ لو كان للقراءة لكان يتكرر بتكرر القراءة ولما لم يكن كذلك بل كرر بتكرر الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.claim: In Eid prayer, Abu Hanifa and Muhammad place the refuge after the extra takbirs, when recitation is about to begin.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.anchor: عندهما أنه يكبر التكبيرات ثم يتعوذ عند القراءة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.claim: Abu Yusuf places seeking refuge before the Eid takbirs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.anchor: وعند أبي يوسف يقدم التعوذ على التكبيرات

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.claim: Measured recitation is Sunnah: articulate letters and words clearly so the reader understands their meanings and conveys them to others; rapid reading prevents understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.anchor: هو أن يذكر الحروف والكلمات مبينة ظاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the Quran's companion is told to read, ascend and recite as he did in worldly life; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r8.anchor: روى أبو داود بإسناده عن ابن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقال لصاحب القرآن اقرأ وارق ورتل

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r9.claim: Al-Khattabi explains that the Quran's verse count corresponds to Paradise's ranks; a reader ascends in proportion to recitation, and one who completes all verses reaches its highest rank.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي : جاء في الأثر أن عدد آي القرآن على عدد درج الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r10.claim: Al-Razi says Quran reading should be performed well and cites an Abu Dawud report from al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, but its wording is cut off in this excerpt.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59#2/r10.anchor: إذا قرأ القرآن فالسنة أن يجيد في القراءة روى أبو داود عن البراء بن عازب قال

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r1.claim: With a full stop after verse 1, idhā introduces an event too terrifying to state directly.
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r1.anchor: When v. 1 is read with a full stop at the end

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r2.claim: Read continuously with verse 2, idhā forms an adverbial clause: when the Event occurs, none can deny its occurrence.
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r2.anchor: If it is read continuously with v. 2, it is considered an adverbial clause

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r3.claim: The verse may refer back to the previous sūrah: its promised blessings for the companions of the right and the foremost arrive when the Event befalls.
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r3.anchor: a reference to the previous sūrah, meaning that all of the blessings promised to the companions of the right and to the foremost

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r4.claim: In either reading, the Event is the eschatological end of the world leading to the Day of Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r4.anchor: the Event refers to the eschatological event of the end of the world leading to the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r5.claim: Al-wāqiʿah derives from waqaʿa, to fall, happen, or occur, expressing inevitability: what must happen will happen.

STUDYQURAN:56:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r7.claim: The Event can also allude to an individual's transformation through sudden or profound spiritual realization.
STUDYQURAN:56:1/r7.anchor: These verses can also be seen as an allusion to individual transformation through sudden or profound spiritual realization.

TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r1.claim: The Event’s arrival is the resurrection cry, when the Trumpet is blown for the Hour.
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r1.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {إذا وقعت الواقعة} [الواقعة: 1] يعني: «الصيحة»

TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the Event as the cry.
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r2.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {إذا وقعت الواقعة} [الواقعة: 1] يعني: «الصيحة»

TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-Wāqiʿa, al-Ṭāmma, and al-Ṣākhkha are names of Resurrection, magnified by God as a warning to His servants.
TAB-FULL:v22p279#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {إذا وقعت الواقعة} [الواقعة: 1] «الواقعة والطامة والصاخة، ونحو هذا من أسماء القيامة، عظمه الله

BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has 99 verses.

BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r2.claim: Idhā is governed by an omitted verb: when the Resurrection rises and occurs at the second trumpet blast, events beyond description will happen.
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r2.anchor: انتصاب إذا بمضمر أي إذا قامت القيامة وحدثت وذلك عند النفخة الثانية يكون من الأهوال

BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r3.claim: Although the Resurrection is future, it is called al-Wāqiʿah, an active participle suggesting the present, because its occurrence is certain; this explains the use of idhā and the past-tense verb.
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r3.anchor: سماها واقعة مع أن دلالة اسم الفاعل على الحال والقيامة مما سيقع في الاستقبال لتحقق وقوعها

BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says waqʿah can stand for battle and for any severe falling.
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب يكنى عن الحرب بالوقعة وكل سقوط شديد يعبر عنه بذلك

BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r5.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Layth says the Resurrection is named al-Wāqiʿah for its sound.
BURSEVI:v9p257#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو الليث سميت القيامة الواقعة لصوتها

TABATABAI:56:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r1.claim: The Meccan sūra depicts the Great Resurrection, its upheavals, the division of people into three groups, their outcomes, arguments against deniers, and death’s approach and final grouping.
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r1.anchor: بيان تصف السورة القيامة الكبرى التي فيها بعث الناس وحسابهم وجزاؤهم

TABATABAI:56:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r2.claim: The sūra is Meccan, as indicated by the context of its verses.

TABATABAI:56:1-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r3.claim: Wuqūʿ is the occurrence of an event; al-wāqiʿa can describe any event, but here means the event of Resurrection.

TABATABAI:56:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r4.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is used as a standalone name for Resurrection, like al-Ḥāqqa, al-Qāriʿa, and al-Ghāshiya.
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r4.anchor: وقد أطلقت إطلاق الأعلام كأنها لا تحتاج إلى موصوف مقدر

TABATABAI:56:1-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r5.claim: The conditional clause has no stated apodosis to magnify the event; its outcome is understood from the sūra’s account of people’s states, approximately that believers prosper and disbelievers lose.
TABATABAI:56:1-4/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر جزاء الشرط إعظاما له وتفخيما لأمره

TABATABAI:56:1/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:1/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:1/r2.claim: The clause about the earth's shaking is appositional to, or explanatory of, “when the Event occurs.”

TABATABAI:56:10/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:10/r14.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:56:10/r14.claim: Al-Zuhri says Ali ibn al-Husayn likened this world and the next to balancing scales, then explained the Event as Resurrection lowering God's enemies into Hell and raising His friends to Paradise.
TABATABAI:56:10/r14.anchor: في الخصال عن الزهري قال سمعت علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يقول

TABATABAI:56:10/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:10/r15.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:56:10/r15.claim: Al-Qummi says the Event is the certain Resurrection and glosses “lowering” as God's enemies and “raising” as His friends.
TABATABAI:56:10/r15.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي { إذا وقعت الواقعة ليس لوقعتها كاذبة } قال القيامة هي حق

TABRISI:56:2-4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:2-4/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:2-4/r11.claim: The first idhā can be governed by the implied verbal meaning of laysa, since the intended sense is that the event's occurrence has no falsehood; another implied governor is also possible.
TABRISI:56:2-4/r11.anchor: إذا وقعت الواقعة ظرف من معنى ليس لأن التقدير لا يكون لوقعتها كاذبة

TABRISI:56:2-4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:2-4/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:2-4/r12.claim: Alternatively, an omitted governor follows from context: when the event occurs, believers win and unbelievers lose.
TABRISI:56:2-4/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون العامل في إذا محذوفا لدلالة الموضع عليه كأنه قال: إذا وقعت الواقعة كذلك فاز المؤمنون

TABRISI:56:2-4/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:2-4/r15.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:56:2-4/r15.claim: Ibn Jinni allows idhā to leave its ordinary adverbial function and begins to cite Labid's line as evidence.
TABRISI:56:2-4/r15.anchor: قال ابن جني: ويجوز أن يفارق إذا الظرفية كقول لبيد:

TABRISI:56:1-16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:1-16/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:56:1-16/r1.claim: Abu al-Hasan analyzes the idhā in the cited Qur'anic phrase as genitive after hatta, so it is not adverbial.
TABRISI:56:1-16/r1.anchor: وقوله سبحانه حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك [يونس: 22] فإذا مجرورة عند أبي الحسن بحتى

TABRISI:56:1-16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:1-16/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:1-16/r2.claim: On that analysis both idhā clauses are nominative, as subject and predicate.
TABRISI:56:1-16/r2.anchor: وأقول فعلى هذا لا يكون قوله إذا ظرفا في الموضعين بل كل واحد منهما في موضع الرفع

TABRISI:56:1-16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:1-16/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:1-16/r3.claim: The author rejects as a grave error a contemporary grammarian's claim that Ibn Jinni made idhā rajjat govern idhā waqaʿat.
TABRISI:56:1-16/r3.anchor: بخلاف ما ظنه بعض المجودين من محققي زماننا في النحو فإنه قال: قال عثمان

TABRISI:56:2-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:2-10/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:56:2-10/r1.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is the Resurrection, also called al-Āzifa; it is the final trumpet blast that starts the Hour.
TABRISI:56:2-10/r1.anchor: أي إذا قامت القيامة عن ابن عباس والواقعة اسم القيامة كالآزفة وغيرها

TABRISI:56:2-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:2-10/r2.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:56:2-10/r2.claim: It is called al-Wāqiʿa because many severe events occur then, or because its impact is exceptionally severe; the phrase urges preparation.
TABRISI:56:2-10/r2.anchor: وقيل: سميت بها لكثرة ما يقع فيها من الشدة أو لشدة وقعها وتقديره اذكروا

THALABI:v9p199#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p199#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p199#3/r1.claim: The Event is the Resurrection, when its morning arrives and the final blast occurs.
THALABI:v9p199#3/r1.anchor: إذا وقعت الواقعة أي إذا نزلت صبيحة القيامة وتلك النفخة الأخيرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:1-10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:1-10/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:1-10/r1.claim: The Event is the coming of the Resurrection.

QASHANI:56:1-3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:56:1-3/r1.claim: Here the Event means the minor resurrection.
QASHANI:56:1-3/r1.anchor: { إذا وقعت الواقعة } أي: القيامة الصغرى { ليس لوقعتها }

ELMALILI:56:1-24/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r1.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa means an event that has occurred and whose occurrence is certain; with the definite article it names the Resurrection because it is sure to come.
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r1.anchor: esasen vukū‘a gelen, vukū‘u muhakkak olan hâdise demektir.

ELMALILI:56:1-24/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r2.claim: Idhā is an adverbial expression that contains a conditional sense.

ELMALILI:56:1-24/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r3.speaker: مفسرون كثيرون
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r3.claim: Many exegetes take the answer to the conditional as omitted for awe, yielding the sense, What tremendous things will happen when Resurrection comes.
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r3.anchor: Çokları cevâbın tehvil için mahzuf olup hâsıl-ı mâna

ELMALILI:56:1-24/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r4.claim: He prefers the apparent construction in which verse 2 supplies the answer to the conditional in verse 1.
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r4.anchor: zâhir olan cevap şudur: {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ}

ELMALILI:56:1-24/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r11.claim: The opening conditional may replace the later when the earth is shaken, depicting it; alternatively it attaches to khāfiḍa and rāfiʿa through tanāzuʿ.
ELMALILI:56:1-24/r11.anchor: bedel olarak onu bir nevi tasvirdir, yahut

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r7.claim: Waqi'a means an important event that occurs and whose occurrence is certain; the term names the Resurrection because its coming is beyond doubt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r7.anchor: vâkıa kelimesi “meydana gelen, vukûu kesin olan önemli hâdise” demektir. Kıyametin geleceğinde kuşku bulunmadığı için bu kelimeyle anılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r8.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r8.claim: Some exegetes hear an implied warning after “when the great event occurs,” such as “you will see what happens.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:1/r8.anchor: “büyük olay gerçekleştiği zaman” ifadesinin devamında “göreceksiniz neler olacak!” gibi bir mânanın bulunduğunu düşünmüşlerdir

QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r1.claim: God's name is overpowering: He brings the attentive near through grace, may remove choice from one persisting in disobedience, and can compel obedience through affliction.
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r1.anchor: من اعتنى بشأنه أحضره بإحسانه ، فإن أبى إلا تماديا في عصيانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r2.claim: The name describes God as eternal, self-subsisting, one, and matchless in beauty and majesty; He is the ally of believers and kind even to sinful believers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r2.anchor: اسم عزيز أزلي ، جبار صمدي ، قهار أحدى ، للمؤمنين ولي ، وبالعاصين حفي

QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r3.claim: When the Resurrection occurs, nothing can repel it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r3.anchor: إذا قامت القيامة لا يردها شيء

QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r5.claim: The person on the path of soundness and uprightness reaches safety and honor; whoever deviates meets regret and loss, and the event distinguishes truth from pretense.
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r5.anchor: ويقال : إذا وقعت الواقعة فمن سلك منهاج الصحة والاستقامة وصل إلى السلامة ولقي الكرامة

QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r6.claim: A poem says that when tears mingle on faces, one can distinguish a genuine mourner from someone pretending to weep.
QUSHAYRI:v3p273/r6.anchor: إذا اشتبكت دموع في خدود . . . تبين من بكى ممن تباكى

BURHAN:v2p386/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r3.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v2p386/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī treats إذا رجت as apposition to إذا وقعت and says the repeated إذا intensifies the close connection between the two constructions.
BURHAN:v2p386/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن جني في قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p199/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p199/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p199/r1.claim: Both إن and إذا introduce a condition and result.
BURHAN:v4p199/r1.anchor: فاما الموافقة فهي إن كل واحد منهما يطلب شرطا وجزاء

BURHAN:v4p199/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p199/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p199/r2.claim: Each requires a verb; when a noun follows, an implicit verb is supplied and explained by the overt one.
BURHAN:v4p199/r2.anchor: وكل واحدة منهما تطلب الفعل فان وقع الاسم بعد واحدة منهما قدر له فعل يرفعه يفسره الظاهر

BURHAN:v4p199/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p199/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p199/r3.claim: إن ordinarily marks an uncertain condition, unlike the certain rising of the sun; it can still describe a certain event whose time is unspecified, as in death.
BURHAN:v4p199/r3.anchor: إلا تدخل إلا على مشكوك نحو إن جئتني اكرمتك ولا يجوز إن طلعت الشمس اتيك لان طلوع الشمس متيقن

BURHAN:v4p199/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p199/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p199/r4.claim: Grammarians say إذا applies to certain events at a definite time; the Qur'an uses it for events whose occurrence is assured.
BURHAN:v4p199/r4.anchor: واما اذا فظاهر كلام النجاة يشعر بانها لاتدخل إلا على المتيقن

ITQAN:v3p283/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r1.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v3p283/r1.claim: Abu Shama classifies sūra openings by form: conditional openings occur in seven sūras, listed in the source.
ITQAN:v3p283/r1.anchor: السادس الشرط في سبع سور الواقعة والمنافقون والتكوير والانفطار والانشقاق والزلزلة والنصر

SULAMI:v2p299/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p299/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p299/r1.claim: When a wayfarer’s path becomes clear, prophetic example leads to the path of Truth, while conjecture and supposition lead to falsehood.
SULAMI:v2p299/r1.anchor: قال سهل : إذا ظهر لكل سالك بيان سلوكه فمن كان سلوكه على منهاج النبوة والاقتداء قاده ذلك

SULAMI:v2p299/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p299/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p299/r2.claim: The Event is when the seeker’s intended purpose becomes clear.
SULAMI:v2p299/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : إذا تبين مراد المريد من مراده

ITQAN:v2p432/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash parses idha in 17:18 as governed in the genitive by hatta.
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش في قوله تعالى ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها ﴾ إن إذا جر بحتى

ITQAN:v2p432/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r2.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v2p432/r2.claim: For accusative readings of khafida and rafiʿa, Ibn Jinni makes the first idha a subject and the second its predicate, with the accusative descriptions as circumstantial clauses; the event lowers some and raises others.
ITQAN:v2p432/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جني في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا وقعت الواقعة ﴾ الآية

ITQAN:v2p432/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.claim: Most grammarians reject taking idha outside its adverbial role: hatta begins the full clause, the second idha apposes the first, and the first has an omitted response inferred as the people dividing into three groups.
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.anchor: والجمهور أنكروا خروجها عن الظرفية وقالوا في الآية الأولى إن حتى حرف ابتداء داخل على الجملة بأسرها

ITQAN:v2p432/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p432/r4.claim: Idha can refer to the present rather than the future when the described action occurs alongside the named time, as with night, day, and the setting star.
ITQAN:v2p432/r4.anchor: فترد للحال نحو ﴿ والليل إذا يغشى ﴾ فإن الغشيان مقارن لليل

ITQAN:v2p432/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p432/r5.claim: Idha can also refer to the past in reports revealed after the events, such as people seeing trade, Dhu al-Qarnayn reaching the sunrise, or building the barrier.
ITQAN:v2p432/r5.anchor: نحو ﴿ وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا ﴾ الآية فإن الآية نزلت بعد الرؤية والانفضاض

ITQAN:v2p432/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p432/r6.claim: In some verses idha is temporal rather than conditional: if it were conditional, a nominal-clause response would require fa; proposed ellipses and alternative parses are rejected as forced or unnecessary.
ITQAN:v2p432/r6.anchor: نحو ﴿ وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون ﴾ ﴿ والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p188/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p188/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p188/r1.claim: When an adjective follows a construct phrase whose first element is a number, it may agree with either the construct head or its complement, as shown by seven heavens in tiers and seven fat cows.
ITQAN:v3p188/r1.anchor: فمن الأول ﴿ سبع سماوات طباقا ﴾ ومن الثاني ﴿ سبع بقرات سمان ﴾

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r1.claim: The image of a docile dog and a thin calf alludes to a host's generosity and hospitality instead of stating those qualities directly.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r1.anchor: لأجل أن أراد أن يذكر نفسه بالقرى والضيافة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r2.claim: Ziyad's tent metonymically locates generosity, manliness, and giving in the praised person, just as the tent is pitched over him.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r2.anchor: راقك بيت زياد لأنه كنى عن إثباته السماحة والمروءة والندى كائنة في الممدوح بجعلها كائنة في القبة المضروبة عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r3.claim: Yazid ibn al-Hakam's poem about Ibn Yazid ibn al-Muhallab in al-Hajjaj's prison gives the captive virtues a setting parallel to the virtues placed in Ziyad's tent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r3.anchor: قول يزيد بن الحكم يمدح بن يزيد بن المهلب وهو في حبس الحجاج

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r4.claim: The phrase about the dog being timid parallels a poem about restraining the dogs from barking: its docility is caused by the household's habitual restraint.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r4.anchor: من حيث لم يكن ذلك الجبن إلا لأن دام منه الزجر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r5.claim: The thin calf allusion parallels Ibn Hurmā's line لا أمتع العوذ بالفصال, another indirect sign of the host's generosity.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r6.claim: Nasib says the patron's dog is more at ease with visitors than a mother with her daughter; the author links this to another poet's image of a dog almost greeting a guest.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p236/r6.anchor: يكاد إذا ما أبصر الضيف مقبلا يكلمه من حبه وهو أعجم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r1.claim: If the challenge were only to produce discourse with rhyme-like endings, the Arabs could do so because they were capable of composing rhymed poetry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r1.anchor: فلو لم يكن التحدي إلا إلى فصول من الكلام يكون لها أواخر أشباه القوافي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r2.claim: The author reports, with reservation about the anecdote's truth, that someone tried to imitate Quranic endings with sections ending in forms such as يعلمون and يؤمنون.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r2.anchor: حتى وضع على ما زعموا فصول كلام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r3.claim: The Quran's inimitability cannot lie in avoiding letter combinations that burden the tongue.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الإعجاز بأن لم يلتق في حروفه ما يثقل على اللسان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r4.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Quran as neither trivial nor incoherent and says entering a Ha Mim sura is like entering lush gardens while tracing their beauties; the author argues this praise is not about meter or endings.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r4.anchor: ابن مسعود حين قال في صفة القرآن : ' لا يتفه ولا يتشان '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r5.claim: The claim that the Quran's marvels never end and do not wear out through repeated recitation cannot be explained by weights or verse-endings alone.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r5.anchor: لا تفنى عجائبه ، ولا يخلق على كثرة الرد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r6.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r6.claim: Al-Jahiz says that even one sura recited to Arab orators would reveal, through its structure and expressive character, their inability to match it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p290/r6.anchor: أم ترى الجاحظ حين قال في كتاب ' النبوة '

DAMGHANI:v1p493/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r5.claim: وقع can mean arose or came to pass; the Occurrence is the Resurrection, and its occurrence means its rising.
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r5.anchor: وقعت أي قامت قوله تعالى في سورة الواقعة إذا وقعت الواقعة أي قامت القيامة ليس لوقعتها أي لقيامتها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r1.claim: Waqaʿa is a past-tense verb; its basic image is falling from a higher place to a lower one.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r1.anchor: وقع : فعل ماض ، والأصل فيه : السقوط من العلو إلى السفل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r2.claim: The phrase waqaʿa kadhā can also mean that something happened; mawāqiʿ al-ghayth are places where rain falls.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r2.anchor: ويقال : وقع كذا ، بمعنى : كان . ومواقع الغيث : مساقطة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r4.claim: In the Hour’s name and the other cited warnings, waqaʿa means occurred or came to pass.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p612/r4.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى كان . ومنه قوله تعالى

MAJAZ:v2p247/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p247/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p247/r1.claim: He identifies al-wāqiʿa with the Hour, which is also called the approaching event in 53:57.
MAJAZ:v2p247/r1.anchor: «إذا وقعت الواقعة» (1) «أزفت الآزفة» (53/ 57) وهى القيامة والساعة..

NAHHAS:v4p321/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p321/r1.claim: Idhā is an accusative time adverb governed by waqaʿat; because it resembles a conditional particle it normally takes what follows as its governor.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r1.anchor: إذا في موضع نصب لأنها ظرف زمان والعامل فيها وقعت لأنها تشبه حروف الشرط

NAHHAS:v4p321/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p321/r2.claim: Sibawayh reports that some Arabs put idhā in the jussive, an analogy to conditionals that is strong but used only in poetry.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r2.anchor: وقد حكى سيبويه أن من العرب من يجزم بها قال وشبهها بحروف الشرط متمكن قوي

NAHHAS:v4p321/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p321/r3.claim: Unlike a conditional, idhā introduces a specified time, as in I will come when the dates redden; the conditional reading cannot use an or similar open-ended timing.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r3.anchor: فأما مخالفتها حروف المجازاة فإن ما بعدها يكون محددا تقول أجيئك إذا حمر البسر ولا يجوز ههنا أن

NAHHAS:v4p321/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p321/r4.claim: The feminine tāʾ in waqaʿat takes kasra to avoid two adjacent sukuns because the particle's default is sukun.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r4.anchor: وكسرت التاء من وقعت لالتقاء الساكنين لأنها حرف فحكمها أن تكون ساكنة

NAHHAS:v4p321/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p321/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says names such as al-Wāqiʿa, al-Tāmma, and al-Ṣākhkha magnify the Resurrection and warn God's servants.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r5.anchor: وروى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال الواقعة والطامة والصاخة ونحو ذلك من أسماء القيامة عظمها الله جل وعز وحذرها عباده

NAHHAS:v4p321/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p321/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p321/r6.claim: Another view identifies al-Wāqiʿa as the first blast.
NAHHAS:v4p321/r6.anchor: وقال غيره هي الصيحة وهي النفخة الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r1.claim: One analysis makes إذا a pure adverb without conditional force, governed by ليس.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها ظرف محض ليس فيه معنى الشرط والعامل فيها " ليس ".

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also offers an adverb governed by an understood اذكر.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: بم انتصبت " إذا "؟ قلت: بليس، كقولك: " يوم الجمعة ليس لي شغل " ثم قال: " أو بإضمار اذكر "

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r3.claim: The Shaykh rejects ليس as adverb-governor because it contains no event; in the Friday example the predicate governs the adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يقول هذا نحوي، ولا من شدا شيئا من صناعة النحو ". قال: " لأن " ليس " مثل " ما " النافية، فلا حدث فيها

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r4.claim: The author says the negation implied by ليس can govern إذا; a verb is closer to event meaning than negative ما.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r4.anchor: قلت: الظروف تعمل فيها روائح الأفعال. ومعنى كلام الزمخشري: أن النفي المفهوم من " ليس " هو العامل في " إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ supports this by taking إذا as governed by what ليس لوقعتها كاذبة conveys.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r5.anchor: قول أبي البقاء: " والثاني ظرف لما دل عليه { ليس لوقعتها كاذبة }

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r6.claim: A conditional analysis has an omitted answer such as كان كيت وكيت; that answer governs إذا.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r6.anchor: الثالث: أنها شرطية. وجوابها مقدر، أي: إذا وقعت كان كيت وكيت، وهو العامل فيها.

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r7.claim: The Shaykh, following Makki, chooses conditional إذا governed by the verb that follows it, وقعت.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2/r7.anchor: الرابع: أنها شرطية، والعامل فيها الفعل الذي بعدها ويليها، وهو اختيار الشيخ، وتبع في ذلك مكيا.

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ makes إذا an adverb of خافضة or رافعة: when the event occurs, it lowers and raises.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r1.anchor: السادس: أنه ظرف ل " خافضة " أو " رافعة " ، قاله أبو البقاء، أي: إذا وقعت

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r2.claim: Another analysis makes إذا an adverb of رجت, with the second إذا either substituting for the first or repeating it.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r2.anchor: السابع: أن يكون ظرفا ل " رجت " " وإذا " الثانية على هذا إما بدل من الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r3.claim: Another analysis governs إذا by what أصحاب الميمنة indicates: when it occurs, people’s conditions arise.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r3.anchor: الثامن: أن العامل فيه ما دل عليه قوله: { فأصحاب الميمنة } ، أي: إذا وقعت

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r4.claim: Another conditional analysis makes فأصحاب الميمنة and what follows the answer.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#2/r4.anchor: التاسع: أن جواب الشرط قوله: { فأصحاب الميمنة } إلى آخره.

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r1.claim: The author praises the explanation that once the event occurs there is no return or reversal.

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r5.claim: The majority read خافضة رافعة nominative as predicates of an omitted subject: it lowers some to Hell and raises others to Paradise, or itself has these qualities.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة برفع " خافضة رافعة " على خبر ابتداء مضمر، أي: هي خافضة قوما إلى النار

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r6.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Muqsim, and al-Yazīdī read خافضة رافعة accusative as circumstantial clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وعيسى والحسن وأبو حيوة وابن مقسم واليزيدي بنصبها على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r7.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r7.claim: A report attributes to al-Kisāʾī the wish to read the accusative if al-Yazīdī had not preceded him; the author doubts it.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r7.anchor: ويروى عن الكسائي أنه قال: " لولا أن اليزيدي سبقني إليه لقرأت به " انتهى. ولا أظن مثل هذا يصح عن مثل هذا.

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r8.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ refers the circumstantial clauses to the pronoun in كاذبة or subject of وقعت; the author corrects his wording because وقعت itself has no pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r8.anchor: وإصلاحه أن يقول: أو فاعل " وقعت " إذ لا ضمير في " وقعت ".

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Faḍl take the circumstantial clauses from الواقعة and allow several from one subject, like several predicates.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وأبو الفضل من

SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r10.speaker: أبو الفضل
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r10.claim: If all are circumstantial clauses, Abū al-Faḍl says an omitted contextual verb governs إذا وقعت, meaning people are judged when it occurs.
SAMIN-DURR:56:1-2#3/r10.anchor: قال أبو الفضل: " وإذا جعلت هذه كلها أحوالا كان العامل في " إذا وقعت " محذوفا يدل عليه الفحوى

ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r1.claim: In Arabic an expected event is said to have occurred just as one says it has come.
ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r1.anchor: يقال لكل آت كان يتوقع قد وقع، تقول: قد وقع الأمر. كقولك قد جاء الأمر

ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p107/r2.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa here is the Hour and Resurrection.

ASAD-NOTES:56:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:1#n1/r1.claim: The event that must come to pass is the Last Hour and Resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:56:1#n1/r1.anchor: I.e. the Last Hour and Resurrection

NASHR:v1p328/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p328/r1.speaker: أصحاب التذكرة
NASHR:v1p328/r1.claim: Al-Tadhkira reports that Ibn Kathīr, Abū Shuʿayb, Qālūn except Abū Nashīṭ, and Yaʿqūb give medium length when a madd letter and hamza share a word, but do not lengthen beyond its intrinsic amount across words.
NASHR:v1p328/r1.anchor: إن ابن كثير، وأبا شعيب وقالون، سوى أبي نشيط ويعقوب - يمدون أحرف المد إذا كن مع الهمزة في كلمة واحدة مدا وسطا

NASHR:v1p328/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p328/r2.speaker: أصحاب التذكرة
NASHR:v1p328/r2.claim: For the other readers, including Abū Nashīṭ from Qālūn and al-Dūrī from Abū ʿAmr, al-Tadhkira reports one extended amount in both contexts, ranked longest for Warsh and Ḥamza, then ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī, then those two routes.
NASHR:v1p328/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وأبو نشيط، عن قالون، والدوري، عن أبي عمرو بمد حرف المد واللين إذا وقعت قبل الهمز في هذين الضربين

NASHR:v1p328/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p328/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p328/r3.claim: Al-Dānī's Taysīr gives short to Ibn Kathīr, Qālūn in one report, and Abū Shuʿayb through al-Yazīdī; others lengthen, with Warsh and Ḥamza longest, followed by ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī, then Abū ʿAmr's Iraqi route and Abū Nashīṭ from Qālūn.
NASHR:v1p328/r3.anchor: إن ابن كثير وقالون - بخلاف عنه - وأبا شعيب وغيره عن اليزيدي يقصرون حرف المد، فلا يزيدونه تمكينا على ما فيه من المد

NASHR:v1p328/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p328/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p328/r4.claim: In al-Jāmiʿ, al-Dānī gives the strongest extension to Ḥamza except Khalaf and to specified Abū Bakr and Ḥafṣ routes; he ranks the remaining routes progressively lower, down to Ibn Kathīr and those distinguishing one word from two.
NASHR:v1p328/r4.anchor: وأشبع القراءة مدا وأزيدهم تمكينا في الضربين جميعا من المتصل والمنفصل حمزة في غير رواية خلاد

NASHR:v1p328/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p328/r5.speaker: أبو محمد مكي
NASHR:v1p328/r5.claim: Makki's Tَبṣira reports short for Ibn Kathīr and Iraqi routes of Abū ʿAmr, and begins its account of Qālūn's routes before the excerpt ends.
NASHR:v1p328/r5.anchor: وقال أبو محمد مكي في التبصرة: إن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو في رواية العراقيين - يعني السوسي والحلواني - عن قالون يقصرون المنفصل

NASHR:v1p464/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p464/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح فارس والداني وصاحب التجريد والشاطبي وأبو العلاء وسبط الخياط
NASHR:v1p464/r1.claim: These authorities and many readers and grammarians permit rum on a final moving hamza after a vowel or long alif when its ending is ḍamma or kasra; the resulting partly voiced vowel licenses between-between easing.
NASHR:v1p464/r1.anchor: فإذا رمت حركة الهمزة في ذلك سهلتها بين بين

NASHR:v1p464/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p464/r2.speaker: جمهور القراء وأكثر النحاة
NASHR:v1p464/r2.claim: Most readers and grammarians reject rum here: at pause the hamza is silent and should be eased like a silent hamza, replaced by the preceding alif; they allow only replacement and treat dammed and kasra endings like fatḥa.
NASHR:v1p464/r2.anchor: وأنكر ذلك جمهورهم وجعلوه مما انفرد به القراء. قالوا: لأن سكون الهمزة في الوقف يوجب فيها الإبدال على الفتحة

NASHR:v1p464/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p464/r3.speaker: أبو العباس المهدوي وأبو عبد الله بن سفيان وأبو الطاهر بن خلف وأبو العز القلانسي وابن الباذش
NASHR:v1p464/r3.claim: These authorities and most grammarians hold that only replacement is allowed; al-Shāṭibī and followers weaken this view and call it anomalous.
NASHR:v1p464/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي العباس المهدوي وأبي عبد الله بن سفيان

NASHR:v1p464/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p464/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p464/r4.claim: The author holds both replacement and rum-with-easing valid: reports from Ḥamza through Khalaf, Sulaym, and Idrīs support rum, while Ibn Wāṣil records additional stopping options; replacement remains the analogical, undisputed option.
NASHR:v1p464/r4.anchor: فدل على صحة الوجهين جميعا، مع أن الإبدال هو القياس، ولم يختلف في صحته

NASHR:v1p464/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p464/r5.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v1p464/r5.claim: The author finds no explicit statement from Sībawayh about this pause case: he says hamza after alif is between-between but does not specify whether that applies at pause or only in connected reading.
NASHR:v1p464/r5.anchor: ولم أر في كلام سيبويه تعرضا إلى هذه المسألة، ولا نص فيها في الوقف بشيء

NASHR:v2p105/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p105/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p105/r1.claim: At pause, final rāʾ follows medial silent rāʾ: it is emphatic after fatḥa or ḍamma and light after kasra; silent yāʾ and imāla before it count like kasra, ishāmām on a raised ending like silence, while rum follows connected reading.
NASHR:v2p105/r1.anchor: أن الراء المتطرفة إذا سكنت في الوقف جرت مجرى الراء الساكنة في وسط الكلمة تفخم بعد الفتحة والضمة

NASHR:v2p105/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p105/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن شريح وأبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p105/r2.claim: For a final rāʾ stopped after a consonant preceded by kasra, where that consonant is emphatic, Ibn Shurayḥ reports emphasis; al-Dānī reports lightening, which the author finds closer to the broader readers' practice.
NASHR:v2p105/r2.anchor: رأيان لأهل الأداء في ذلك فعلى التفخيم نص الإمام أبو عبد الله بن شريح

NASHR:v2p105/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p105/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p105/r3.claim: For the examples Miṣr and Qaṣr, the author chooses emphasis in Miṣr but lightening in Qaṣr, considering connected pronunciation and the original rule.
NASHR:v2p105/r3.anchor: لكني أختار في مصر التفخيم، وفي (قصر) الترقيق

NASHR:v2p105/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p105/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p105/r4.claim: When stopping on bisharar for readers who lighten its first rāʾ, the second is also light despite following fatḥa, by reciprocal lightening analogous to imāla for imāla.
NASHR:v2p105/r4.anchor: إذا وقفت بالسكون على بشرر لمن يرقق الراء الأولى رققت الثانية وإن وقعت بعد فتح

NASHR:v2p105/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p105/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p105/r5.claim: The author rejects Makki's reported emphasis for Warsh on words such as al-nār at pause with imāla: the rāʾ should remain light because of imāla, whether pausing silently or with rum.
NASHR:v2p105/r5.anchor: بل الصواب الترقيق من أجل الإمالة سواء أسكنت أم رمت لا نعلم في ذلك خلافا

NASHR:v2p117/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p117/r1.speaker: إبراهيم بن عمر الجعبري وعبد الله بن عبد المؤمن الواسطي
NASHR:v2p117/r1.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī and al-Wāsiṭī say the divine name is emphatic after an un-kasraed light letter, as in yubashshir Allāh; after major imāla, as in narā Allāha, either emphasis or lightening is allowed.
NASHR:v2p117/r1.anchor: إذا وقعت بعد ترقيق خال من الكسر فهي على تفخيمها نحو يبشر الله عباده، أو بعد إمالة كبرى فوجهان

NASHR:v2p117/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p117/r2.speaker: بعض أهل الأداء من أهل عصرنا
NASHR:v2p117/r2.claim: An unnamed contemporary performance authority proposes lightening the divine name after a light rāʾ, analogizing that rāʾ to imāla and arguing that ḍamma can be imāla too, despite not receiving the reading from a teacher.
NASHR:v2p117/r2.anchor: بلغنا عنه أنه رأى ترقيق اسم الله تعالى بعد الراء المرققة فأجرى الراء المرققة في ذلك مجرى الراء الممالة

NASHR:v2p117/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p117/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p117/r3.claim: The author rejects that analogy: in مذعور the ḍamma itself approaches kasra, but in yubashshir Allāh only rāʾ is lightened; the ḍamma stays unchanged. Lightening rāʾ differs from imāla, so narā Allāha is no precedent.
NASHR:v2p117/r3.anchor: والضمة التي هي على الراء في يبشر لم تقرب إلى الكسرة، ولا غيرت عن حالتها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p269/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p269/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p269/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the event's having no “kādhiba” with the word “mathnūya,” indicating no turning back or denial of its occurrence.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p269/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا وقعت الواقعة ﴾ قال نزلت ﴿ ليس لوقعتها كاذبة ﴾ قال مثنوية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p74/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p74/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p74/r13.claim: The sūra is Meccan and follows al-Raḥmān, which paired punishment for sinners with bliss for believers; its two pairs of gardens distinguish lower- and higher-ranking believers, matching the three groups named at this sūra’s start and the groups at its end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p74/r13.anchor: هذه السورة مكية، ومناسبتها لما قبلها تضمن العذاب للمجرمين، والنعيم للمؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-Wāqiʿa is one of the Resurrection’s names, like al-Ṣākhkha, al-Ṭāmma, and al-Āzifa; these names convey its gravity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الواقعة من أسماء القيامة، كالصاخة والطامة والآزفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r3.claim: The phrase means that the event which must occur has happened; wuqūʿ is the descent or arrival of what one awaited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r3.anchor: ومعنى وقعت الواقعة: أي وقعت التي لا بد من وقوعها، كما تقول: حدثت الحادثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r4.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies al-Wāqiʿa as the blast, the trumpet’s blowing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الواقعة: الصيحة، وهي النفخة في الصور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r5.claim: Another view says it is the rock of Jerusalem that falls on the Day of Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r5.anchor: وقيل: الواقعة: صخرة بيت المقدس تقع يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r6.claim: He says the following verb is the syntactic governor of idhā; because no spoken conditional answer appears to govern it, a governing element must be estimated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r6.anchor: والعامل في إذا الفعل بعدها على ما قررناه في كتب النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī proposes that idhā is accusative through laysa, an omitted clause such as ‘when it occurs, such-and-such will happen,’ or an implicit udhkur, ‘remember.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p75/r7.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: بم انتصب إذا؟ قلت: بليس، كقولك: يوم الجمعة ليس لي شغل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r1.claim: If idhā is conditional and the response begins with laysa, it requires fāʾ, except under poetic license; thus the plain response without fāʾ is not valid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r1.anchor: ولو كانت شرطا، وكان الجواب الجملة المصدرة بليس، لزمت الفاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s Friday example treats idhā without its usual conditional force; his omitted-answer proposal, by contrast, treats it as conditional, while his udhkur proposal makes it an object rather than an adverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p76/r2.anchor: ويظهر من تمثيل الزمخشري إذا بقوله: يوم الجمعة، أنه سلبها الدلالة على الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77/r7.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77/r7.claim: If all are circumstantial clauses, al-Rāzī says the governor of idhā waqaʿat is omitted and inferred from the context, such as yuḥāsabūn, ‘they are judged.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77/r7.anchor: وإذا جعلت هذه كلها أحوالا، كان العامل في إذا وقعت محذوفا يدل عليه الفحوى بتقدير يحاسبون ونحوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r9.speaker: ابن جني وأبو الفضل الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jinnī and Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī treat idhā rajjat as a nominative predicate of idhā waqaʿat, with both idhās meaning ‘the time when,’ not forming conditions; the author says his syntax retains the conditional sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جني وأبو الفضل الرازي: إذا رجت في موضع رفع على أنه خبر للمبتدأ الذي هو إذا وقعت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r10.speaker: ابن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r10.claim: Ibn Mālik cites the construction as evidence that idhā can be a subject; Abū Ḥayyān says he has explained how to preserve its conditional meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p77#2/r10.anchor: وهكذا ادعى ابن مالك أن إذا تكون مبتدأ، واستدل بهذا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r1.claim: وقعت means happened, and الواقعة is a conventional name or transferred name for the Resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly identifies الواقعة as one of the names of the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r2.anchor: وصرح ابن عباس بأنها من أسمائها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r3.claim: The name signals that the Resurrection’s occurrence is certain, as though it had already happened independently of the conditional clause; this is not a vacuous subject-verb repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r3.anchor: وسميت بذلك للإيذان بتحقق وقوعها لا محالة كأنها واقعة في نفسها مع قطع النظر عن الوقوع الواقع في حيز الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r4.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies الواقعة as the cry, meaning the blast in the trumpet.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك : ( الواقعة ) الصيحة وهي النفخة في الصور

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r5.claim: Another view says it is the rock of Jerusalem that will fall on Judgment Day; the author calls this baseless.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r5.anchor: وقيل : ( الواقعة ) صخرة بيت المقدستقع يوم القيامة وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan treats إذا as a conditional time adverb governed by the following verb وقعت, like other conditional nouns, and says it is not annexed to the clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r6.anchor: والعامل فيها عند أبي حيان الفعل بعدها فهي عنده في موضع نصب بوقعت

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r7.claim: Most grammarians treat إذا as annexed to the following clause; one view says it loses its adverbial force and is an object of an omitted ذكر.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r7.anchor: والجمهور على إضافتها فقيل : هي هنا قد سلبت الظرفية ووقعت مفعولا به

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r8.claim: Another analysis preserves its adverbial force and makes ليس its governor, which the author says al-Zamakhshari’s wording seems to favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r8.anchor: وقيل : لم تسلب ذلك وهي منصوبة بليس وصنيع الزمخشري يشعر باختياره

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r9.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r9.claim: Al-Kashf prefers an omitted answer as the governor, understood as when the Event occurs, such-and-such will happen; the omission magnifies the event.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r9.anchor: وقيل : بمحذوفوهو الجواب أي ( إذا وقعتالواقعة )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that no grammarian makes ليس govern the adverb, since it resembles ما and lacks event or temporal meaning; he also says a conditional answer with ليس requires fā.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r10.anchor: وأبو حيان تعقب النصب بليس لا يذهب إليه نحوي لأن ليس في النفي ك ( ما ) وهي لا تعمل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r11.claim: A rebuttal notes that grammarians allow an adverb to attach to ما by interpreting it as انتفى, and apply the same reasoning to ليس.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r11.anchor: صرحوا بجواز تعلق الظرف بها لتأويلها بانتفي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r12.claim: The author answers that fā is obligatory with the answer to إن because of its operation, whereas its use with إذا is contrary to the default.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r12.anchor: بأن لزوم الفاء مع الأفع الالجامدة إنما هو في جواب إن الشرطية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r13.claim: After the grammatical debate, the author prefers an omitted answer as the governor; leaving it unspecified creates awe and magnifies the Event.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p129/r13.anchor: الأولى كون العامل محذوفاوهو الجواب كما سمعت وفي إبهامه تهويل وتفخيم لأمر الواقعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r1.claim: When the Event occurs, the Resurrection will have begun.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r2.claim: Another view identifies the Event as the final blast of the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p7#4/r2.anchor: وقيل: إذا نزلت صيحة القيامة وهي النفخة الأخيرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.claim: The al-wāqiʿa is the Resurrection; its name signals that it will certainly occur.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.anchor: إذا حدثت القيامة، سماها واقعة لتحقق وقوعها

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.claim: The temporal clause is governed by an omitted command such as ‘remember,’ or an implied statement that such-and-such will happen.

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Some lexical patterns are kept intact because they do not follow a verb pattern; surrounding consonant quiescence also favors retention, as with gemination before a quiescent consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: لأنه ليس على مثال الفعل فيمثل به ولكنه أتم لسكون ما قبله وما بعده

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Many derived noun patterns retain wāw or yāʾ rather than hamzating them; Sībawayh lists forms such as ʿawār, qawwāl, and miqwāl.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وذلك فعل وفعال نحو حول وعوار وكذلك فعال نحو قوال ومفعال نحو مشوار

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Some Arabs say abyanāʾ, with a quiescent yāʾ and a vowel on bāʾ to avoid kasra on yāʾ; Sībawayh says this is not regular.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وقد قال بعض ~~العرب أبيناء فأسكن الياء وحرك الباء كره الكسرة في الياء

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: The verbal nouns iqāma and istiqāma are defective because they remain closely tied to their derived verbs; as independent triliteral verbal nouns, they would retain the full form.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: الإقامة والاستقامة فإنما اعتلتا كما اعتلت أفعالهما لأن لزوم الاستفعال

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: The passive participle mafʿūl is shortened and made quiescent because it is the noun of its verb, so it follows the verb in defectiveness; other cited forms are not verb-nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وأما مفعول فإنهم حذفوه فيهما وأسكنوه لأنه الاسم من

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Ṭawīl is not formed on yaṭūlu; if it were the verb-based noun, it would be ṭāʾil. It instead patterns as faʿīl with a passive sense and preserves the root, as in makhyūṭ.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: فإن طويلا لم يجئ على يطول ولا على الفعل ألا ترى أنك لو أردت

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Maqāwil and maʿāyish are not hamzated because they are plurals of maqāla and maʿīša, whose original vowels remain; they are not nouns patterned on the verb.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: ولم يهمزوا مقاول ومعايش لأنهما ليستا بالاسم على الفعل

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Khalīl explains that mafʿal is retained because it is essentially shortened from mifʿāl; the patterns share adjectival meaning and can alternate, as in maftaḥ and miftāḥ.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وسألته عن مفعل لأي شيء أتم

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Sībawayh calls maṣāʾib an error from treating maṣība as faʿīla; it is mafʿila, and maṣāwib is also attested.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وذلك أنهم توهموا أن مصيبة فعيلة

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: The weak radicals in ʿajūz, risāla, and ṣaḥīfa are hamzated in their plurals because they are originally quiescent, unlike roots that take vowels; after alif they are especially liable to hamza.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: وسألته عن واو عجوز وألف رسالة وياء صحيفة لأي شيء همزن في الجمع

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: The fāʿil forms from ʿawirat and ṣīdat are ʿāwir and ṣāyid, preserving their weak radicals as in šawayt and ḥayiyt, though assimilation does not apply.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: فاعل من عورت فإذا قالوا فاعل غدا

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: Fawāʿil plurals from ʿawirat and ṣīdat take hamza by analogy with šawāyā and other hamzated plurals; the heavy meeting of two wāws also supports the change.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: فإذا قلت فواعل من عورت وصيدت همزت لأنك تقول في شويت شوايا

SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.speaker: author
