SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.claim: When a noun is formed first and then pluralized, as in taqāwul and tabāyuʿ, hamza is not introduced: the weak radical was originally vowelled, as in maʿūna and maʿīša.
SIBAWAYH:(لأنهليسعلىمثالالفعلفيمثلبهولكن.anchor: لو كانت تقول اسما ثم أردت أن تكسر للجمع لقلة تقاول

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.claim: After al-Raḥmān classified criminals, forerunners, and followers and closed with retribution and honor, this sūra unfolds their afterlife conditions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.anchor: لما صنف سبحانه الناس في تلك إلى ثلاث أصناف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is the second blast, bringing the universal resurrection and assembly of all creatures for judgment under God’s manifest, unshared rule.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.anchor: وهي النفخة الثانية التي يكون عنها البعث الأكبر الذي هو القيامة الجامعة لجميع الخلق للحكم بينهم على الانفراد الظاهر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.claim: The definite article signals perfection: no event deserves the complete name “the Occurrence” as fully as the Resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.anchor: ولا واقع يستحق أن يسمى الواقعة بلام الكمال وتاء المبالغة غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.claim: The conditional “when” may be attached to an omitted predicate, leaving the mind to imagine the awe-inspiring events that follow.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.anchor: منصوبا بالمحذوف لتذهب النفس فيه كل مذهب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r18.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r18.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the two preceding sūras presented decisive proofs, while the close of al-Qamar taught that every worldly event occurs by God’s decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p402#2/r18.anchor: أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم الإعذار في السورتين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the close of al-Qamar’s decree teaching to its cited verses, then says al-Wāqiʿa opens by making the afterlife division explicit.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r1.anchor: وأعلمهم سبحانه في الواقعة بانقسامهم الأخروي فافتتح ذكر الساعة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r2.claim: He contrasts this sūra’s full, explicit account of afterlife states with the earlier sūras’ worldly instruction and subtler allusions; its ending confirms the final recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p404/r2.anchor: فتجردت هذه السورة للتعريف بأحوالهم الأخروية

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan and has ninety-six verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها ست وتسعون بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat al-Waqi'a was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr likewise says Surat al-Waqi'a was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r3.anchor: ابن مردويه عن ابن الزبير مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r4.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites Surat al-Waqi'a every night will never suffer poverty.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: من قرأ سورة الواقعة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the same promise that nightly recitation of Surat al-Waqi'a prevents poverty.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من قرأ سورة الواقعة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r6.claim: Anas reports the Prophet calling Surat al-Waqi'a the sura of wealth and urging that it be recited and taught to children.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r6.anchor: عن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سورة الواقعة سورة الغنى

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r7.claim: A report from Anas says the Prophet urged teaching Surat al-Waqi'a to women because it is the sura of wealth.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: علموا نساءكم سورة الواقعة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r8.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r8.claim: Aisha urged women not to neglect reciting Surat al-Waqi'a.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r8.anchor: عن سليمان التيمي قال: قالت عائشة للنساء: لا تعجز إحداكن أن تقرأ سورة الواقعة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r9.claim: Jabir ibn Samura says the Prophet used to recite al-Waqi'a and similar suras in the dawn prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن سمرة قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقرأ في الفجر الواقعة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet regularly recited al-Waqi'a and other suras; when Abu Bakr noted his rapid graying, the Prophet said Hud and its sister suras had made him gray.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ألظ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الواقعة والحاقة

DURR-FULL:v8p3/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-Waqi'a as the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p3/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {إذا وقعت الواقعة} قال: يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v8p6/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p6/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p6/r9.claim: Jabir ibn Abdullah says Umar asked about a group from the first and a group from the last; the Prophet called Adam and his community groups and said his community’s group would be completed when they sought aid.
DURR-FULL:v8p6/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت {إذا وقعت الواقعة} ذكر فيها {ثلة من الأولين وقليل من الآخرين}

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3329/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3329/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3329/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the Inevitable Event as the Day of Resurrection and says it cannot be turned back.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3329/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : اذا وقعت الواقعة قال : يوم القيامة ليس لوقعتها كاذبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r1.claim: The feminine form of al-waqi'a follows an implied feminine noun such as event, occurrence, or Hour, a common Arabic usage also seen in the expression the circle turned on them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r1.anchor: فراعوا في تأنيثها معنى الحادث أو الكائنة أو الساعة ، وهو تأنيث كثير في اللغة جار على ألسنة العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r2.claim: Al-Waqi'a refers to the Resurrection and has become its established Quranic name, like al-Sakhkha, al-Tamma, and al-Azifa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r2.anchor: والمراد بالواقعة هنا القيامة فجعل هذا الوصف علما لها بالغلبة في اصطلاح القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r3.claim: Repeating the root of al-Waqi'a in its verb creates paronomasia.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p281/r3.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار صار في قوله : { إذا وقعت الواقعة } محسن التجنيس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies al-Wāqiʿa as the Resurrection; its other names signify gravity and terror.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r1.anchor: الواقعة: اسم من أسماء القيامة ك الصاعقة [البقرة: 55، النساء: 153] والآزفة [غافر: 18، النجم: 57] والطامة [النازعات: 34] قاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says al-Wāqiʿa is the cry, meaning the blast of the Trumpet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الواقعة: الصيحة وهي النفخة في الصور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes say it is the Rock of Jerusalem, which falls at the Resurrection; all these interpretations concern the Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p238#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: الواقعة: صخرة بيت المقدس، تقع عند القيامة، فهذه كلها معان لأجل القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r1.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī says the verse came after the polytheists asked when the promised event and victory would occur.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الدمشقي لما قال المشركون متى هذا الوعد متى هذا الفتح نزل قوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r2.claim: The exegetes identify al-wāqiʿa as the Resurrection; the name suits any certain future event once it has occurred, and here refers to the Trumpet blast that begins the Hour.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p130/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون والواقعة القيامة وكل آت يتوقع يقال له إذا كان قد وقع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p513#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p513#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p513#2/r1.claim: Al-Waqiʿa is a name for the Resurrection because its occurrence is certain and real, as 69:15 also says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p513#2/r1.anchor: الواقعة: من أسماء يوم القيامة، سميت بذلك لتحقق كونها ووجودها، كما قال:

JISHUMI:v9p6737/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has ninety-six verses.

JISHUMI:v9p6737/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r2.speaker: مسروق
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r2.claim: Masrūq reports from Ibn Masʿūd that anyone seeking news of earlier and later peoples, Paradise, Hell, and the Hereafter should recite al-Wāqiʿa; no grade is stated.
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r2.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود عن مسروق: (من أراد أن يعلم نبأ الأولين والآخرين، ونبأ أهل الجنة، ونبأ أهل النار

JISHUMI:v9p6737/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r3.claim: After al-Raḥmān closed with promise and Paradise, this sūra opens with the Resurrection and Paradise and arranges people's ranks.
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r3.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الرحمن) بالوعد، وصفة الجنة، افتتح هذه السورة بصفة القيامة والجنة، ورتب فيها درجات الناس.

JISHUMI:v9p6737/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r5.claim: Waqʿ is the appearance of something through occurrence, like a falling object appearing before an observer; the feminine is wāqiʿa.
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r5.anchor: الوقع: ظهور الشيء بالحدوت، كظهور الساقط بحضرة الرائي، وقع يقع وقوعا، وهو واقع، والأنثى واقعة.

JISHUMI:v9p6737/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r9.claim: The verb governing إذا is omitted; the implied command is “Remember when the Event occurs.”
JISHUMI:v9p6737/r9.anchor: العامل في إذا محذوف، تقديره: اذكر إذا وقعت الواقعة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r1.claim: The Event is the Resurrection, called an occurrence because it will certainly happen; وقع means something descended or came to pass.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r2.claim: إذا is governed by ليس, an omitted verb meaning such-and-such will happen, or an implied command to remember.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p454/r2.anchor: فإن قلت : بم انتصب إذا ؟ قلت : بليس . كقولك يوم الجمعة ليس لي شغل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says al-waqi'a is the blast or cry.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says it is the Hour, which has truly occurred and cannot be denied.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan identify al-waqi'a as the Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r4.claim: It is called al-waqi'a because of the many ordeals occurring during it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p445#2/r4.anchor: وسميت الواقعة لكثرة ما يقع فيها من الشدائد

MUQATIL:56:1-2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:1-2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:1-2/r1.claim: The Event is the first blast, a cry.
MUQATIL:56:1-2/r1.anchor: يعني إذا وقعت الصيحة، وهي النفخة الأولى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r1.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is the Resurrection; alternatively, it is named for its certain occurrence, meaning when the inevitable event happens.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r1.anchor: قامت القيامة وقيل وصفت بالوقوع لانها تقع لام محالة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r2.claim: Waqaʿa can mean that a matter descends or arrives, as in “what I expected has come.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r2.anchor: ووقع الامر نزوله يقال وقع ما كنت اتوقعه اى نزل ما كنت اترقب نزوله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p206/r3.claim: The temporal particle idhā is governed by an omitted verb of remembering.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.claim: The Event is the Resurrection, specifically the final blast.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r1.anchor: أي قامت القيامة، والمراد النفخة الأخيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.claim: It is called al-Wāqiʿa because it will occur soon.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r2.anchor: وسميت واقعة لأنها تقع عن قرب

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r3.claim: Another explanation derives its name from the many calamities that will occur during it.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r3.anchor: وقيل: لكثرة ما يقع فيها من الشدائد

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r4.claim: The clause has an ellipsis: remember when the Event occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r4.anchor: وفيه إضمار، أي اذكروا إذا وقعت الواقعة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r5.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Jurjānī treats idhā as an extra particle, like the formulations in 54:1 and 16:1; he compares it to saying the fast has come when it is near.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r5.anchor: وقال الجرجاني: «إذا» صلة أي وقعت الواقعة كقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r6.claim: On the first analysis, idhā marks time and the response is “then the people of the right.”
QURTUBI-FULL:56:1-3/r6.anchor: وعلى الأول «إذا» للوقت، والجواب قوله: { فأصحب الميمنة مآ أصحب الميمنة }
